title: Why Can't You Ever Reach a Rainbow? #rainbow #physics
description:
A rainbow isn't a thing in the sky: it's an angle. Light leaving raindrops bunches up about 42° from the path the sunlight came in on, so you only see colour from drops about 42° from the shadow of your head. Move, and a different set of drops lights up.

Full episode: Why is a rainbow always at the same angle? https://youtu.be/CywvAndxdSk

Sources
- HyperPhysics (Georgia State University), Rainbow
- Cowley, Atmospheric Optics, Rainbows
- Nussenzveig (1977), The theory of the rainbow, Scientific American 236(4)
- Minnaert, Light and Colour in the Outdoors, Springer

Have you ever seen a double rainbow? Tell me in the comments.
